script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Morning, Sarah. August 10th already. Can you believe it?
script.ja: おはようございます、サラさん。もう8月10日ですね。信じられますか？

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: Morning, Alex. No, time goes fast.
script.ja: おはよう、アレックス。うん、時間はあっという間ね。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Yeah. Need my coffee today. Always need it, but especially with this weather.
script.ja: ええ。今日はコーヒーが要りますね。いつもそうなんですけど、この天気だと特に。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: It's pretty gloomy out there.
script.ja: 外はかなりどんよりしてるわね。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: It is. They're saying 100% chance of rain. And 26 degrees? Feels colder than that, somehow.
script.ja: そうですね。降水確率100%だって。26度？なぜかそれより寒く感じます。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: Well, low is 21.5. So, not exactly summer anymore.
script.ja: まあ、最低気温は21.5度だからね。もう夏って感じじゃないわね。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Yeah, feels like autumn is trying to push its way in. It's too early for that.
script.ja: ええ、秋が割り込もうとしているみたい。まだ早すぎますよ。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: Did you see the news about Fukushima? Rebuilding with fish and tomatoes and hula-dancing girls.
script.ja: 福島のニュース見た？魚とトマトと、フラダンサーの女の子たちで復興してるって。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Hula-dancing girls? That's quite a mix. I mean, good for them, rebuilding. It's been a long time since 2011.
script.ja: フラダンサーですか？すごい組み合わせですね。まあ、復興してるのはいいことですよね。2011年からずいぶん経ちましたもんね。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: It has. It's good to see positive stories from there.
script.ja: そうね。そこから良い話が聞けるのは嬉しいわ。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Yeah, my parents visited a few years ago. Said it was really coming back. I just hope the fish are okay.
script.ja: ええ、うちの両親が数年前に訪れたんですよ。かなり復興しているって言ってました。魚だけは大丈夫だといいんですけど。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: They are very careful about that now.
script.ja: 今はその辺り、とても気をつけてるから大丈夫よ。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Oh, this one, though. Japan's food self-sufficiency rate, 37%. Record low. That's not great, is it?
script.ja: あ、でもこれですよ。日本の食料自給率、37%だって。過去最低。これ、良くないですよね？

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: No, it's not. It worries me a bit, actually. Especially with global events.
script.ja: ええ、良くないわね。正直、少し心配になるわ。特に世界情勢を考えると。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Yeah. I mean, my office isn't going to start farming on the roof, so I don't know what we can do about that.
script.ja: ええ。うちの会社が屋上で農業を始めるわけじゃないし、どうしたらいいのかって思っちゃいますね。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: It's a national issue.
script.ja: それは国家的な問題よ。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Right. I just feel like I read this headline every year. It keeps getting lower.
script.ja: そうですね。毎年この見出しを読んでる気がします。どんどん下がっていってる。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: It does.
script.ja: そうね。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: There's also something about ukiyo-e tarot cards. East-meets-West.
script.ja: それと、浮世絵のタロットカードの話もあったわね。東洋と西洋の融合ってやつ。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Tarot cards? Like, fortune telling? I didn't know that was big in Japan.
script.ja: タロットカード？占いみたいなやつですか？日本でそんなに人気があるとは知りませんでした。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: It became popular after World War II. And ukiyo-e, of course, is a very Japanese art style. So, it makes sense.
script.ja: 第二次世界大戦後に人気が出たのよ。そして浮世絵はもちろん、とても日本的な芸術様式だから、納得できるわね。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Huh. My wife would probably like those. She's into that kind of thing. She's been a bit moody lately, you know, with the baby's tantrums.
script.ja: へえ。うちの妻、たぶん好きだと思いますよ。ああいうの好きなんです。最近ちょっと機嫌が悪いというか、ほら、赤ちゃんが癇癪をね。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: Oh? What kind of tantrums?
script.ja: あら？どんな癇癪なの？

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Just, you know, when he gets upset and screams and won't calm down. It's like he's just expressing himself, but it's intense. I mean, he's just over a year old. Is "tantrum" the right word for a baby?
script.ja: もう、あの、機嫌が悪くなって叫んだり、落ち着かなかったりするんです。自分を表現してるだけなんでしょうけど、激しいんですよ。まだ1歳ちょっとですし。「tantrum」って、赤ちゃんにも使う言葉ですか？

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: Yes, it is. A `tantrum` is when a child, usually a young child, gets very angry or frustrated and expresses it by crying loudly, yelling, or hitting things.
script.ja: ええ、そうよ。`tantrum`（癇癪）というのは、子ども、特に小さい子が、とても怒ったり、不満を感じたりして、大声で泣いたり、叫んだり、物を叩いたりしてそれを表現することね。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Ah, okay. That's exactly it. He's a very expressive little guy.
script.ja: ああ、なるほど。まさにそれです。うちの子は感情表現豊かな子なので。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Speaking of holidays, it's Yama no Hi today, right? Mountain Day.
script.ja: 祝日といえば、今日って山の日ですよね？

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: That's right. August 10th.
script.ja: その通りよ。8月10日。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: I always forget which day it is, or why. It's a newer holiday, isn't it? Since 2016?
script.ja: いつも何の日かとか、なぜなのか忘れちゃうんですよ。比較的新しい祝日でしたっけ？2016年から？

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: Yes, the 16th national holiday. It's for appreciating mountains and getting closer to them.
script.ja: ええ、16番目の国民の祝日よ。山に親しむ機会を得て、山の恩恵に感謝することが目的ね。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: I guess that's nice. I don't really climb mountains. My idea of "getting close" is maybe seeing one from a train.
script.ja: まあ、いいことだと思います。僕はあまり山に登ったりしないですけどね。「親しむ」っていうのは、電車から山を見るくらいかなあ。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: Most people don't climb them on a holiday, I think.
script.ja: ほとんどの人が祝日に山に登ったりはしないと思うわ。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Yeah. My kids would probably complain about the `rigor` of it all. Like, "Dad, are we there yet?" every five minutes.
script.ja: ええ。うちの子どもたちは、きっとその大変さに文句を言うでしょうね。5分おきに「パパ、まだ着かないの？」とか。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: The... the `rigor` of climbing. Is that the right word?
script.ja: その…登山の『rigor』。その言葉で合ってる？

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: `Rigor` means the difficulty and strictness of something, or how challenging it is physically or mentally. So, yes, the physical difficulty of climbing.
script.ja: `Rigor`（厳しさ）とは、何かの困難さや厳格さ、あるいはそれが肉体的にも精神的にもどれほど挑戦的か、という意味よ。だから、ええ、登山の肉体的な困難さ、で合ってるわ。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Got it. Yeah, my son especially. He doesn't like anything too challenging. My daughter is a bit more adventurous.
script.ja: なるほど。ええ、特に息子がそうです。彼はあまり大変なことが好きじゃないんです。娘の方はもう少し冒険好きなんですけどね。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: Teenagers are like that.
script.ja: ティーンエイジャーってそんなものよ。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Anyway, with all this rain, maybe it's a good day for an indoor activity. I was thinking about going to the sento this weekend.
script.ja: ところで、こんな雨だと、室内での活動がいいかもしれませんね。今週末、銭湯に行こうかと思ってて。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: That sounds nice.
script.ja: それはいいわね。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Yeah, just to get that `totonou` feeling. You know? You sit in the sauna, then the cold bath, then relax. It's quiet.
script.ja: ええ、あの『ととのう』感じを味わいたくて。サウナに入って、水風呂、それから休憩。静かで。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: I understand. A lot of people enjoy that.
script.ja: わかるわ。多くの人があれを楽しむわね。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Yeah, it's my escape sometimes. The baby's just started walking, so the house is always a bit chaotic. I need some quiet time after a few `consecutive` days of that.
script.ja: ええ、僕にとって時々、逃げ場なんです。赤ちゃんが歩き始めたばかりで、家の中がいつもちょっと混沌としてて。何日か続けてそんな状態だと、静かな時間が欲しくなるんです。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: `Consecutive` days. Is that the right word?
script.ja: 『consecutive』な日々。その言葉で合ってる？

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Yes. `Consecutive` means following one after another without interruption. So, several days in a row.
script.ja: ええ。『consecutive』（連続した）というのは、途切れることなく次から次へと続く、という意味よ。だから、何日も連続して、ということね。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Okay. It feels like many days in a row sometimes. My wife says I need to relax more.
script.ja: なるほど。時には何日も連続してるように感じます。妻も僕にもっとリラックスしろって言うんですよ。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: Taking time for yourself is important.
script.ja: 自分の時間を持つことは大切よ。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: So, are you planning anything for Mountain Day, Sarah?
script.ja: それで、山の日、サラさんは何か予定ありますか？

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: Not really. Maybe a nice cup of tea.
script.ja: 特にないわね。美味しいお茶でも飲むくらいかしら。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Sounds very Sarah-like. Mine will definitely be coffee.
script.ja: いかにもサラさんらしいですね。僕は間違いなくコーヒーです。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Well, that's it for us on The Daily Tanu-chan Show this morning. Thanks for listening!
script.ja: さて、今朝の『The Daily Tanu-chan Show』はここまでです。お聴きいただきありがとうございました！

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: Thank you.
script.ja: ありがとうございました。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: We'll be back tomorrow. Have a good one!
script.ja: また明日お会いしましょう。良い一日を！

wikipedia.description: 16番目の祝日として2016年に施行。「山に親しむ機会を得て、山の恩恵に感謝する」ことが目的。
